If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% in mid-horizon (days 11–20) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 3–7% in late horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 3–7% in early horizon to offset pessimism.  
If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) and forecast is below historical mean, increase forecast by 5–10% in mid-horizon to align with sentiment momentum.
